texts: In the late summer of Year 1, one day before the autumn equinox, Meren Tallowhand walked to a station on the Cliff Path at sundown.
Meren Tallowhand lit the lantern at the station.
The lantern showed mist-light at night.
Meren Tallowhand tended the lantern that night.
Meren Tallowhand counted seventeen nightmoths at the lantern at the third watch.
A handful of nightmoths gathered at the Middle Row that night.
All the sky-cats stayed on the cliff-spires that night.

q1_issues.issue: "The mist-light" is given a fresh witness sk_mist_light_1 while the same substance is the bare constant mist_light in the two preceding statements (indices 28 and 33), so the anaphoric definite is severed from its antecedent and the attracting is predicated of a different symbol than the producing.
"the Middle Row" gets its Name atom but no type atom, although the kind word sits inside the name exactly as in "the Cliff Path", which the same parse types with (Member cliff_path path).

q2_gaps: a non-deictic season expression anchored to a stated year ("in the late summer of Year 1") - Time defines Year/Month/Day/Weekday/Hour/Minute terms plus speech-anchored season deictics (last_spring, next_summer), but no form for a season of a named year, so the parse invents the bare constant late_summer beside (Year 1)
a named watch division of the night ("at the third watch") - no licensed Time term covers watch periods; only day-part constants (dawn/noon/dusk/night) and fiscal-period terms are defined
review.notes: Event structure, roles, the BeforeBy gap for "one day before the autumn equinox", the handful/seventeen count encodings and the "all the sky-cats" distribution rule with its QuantifierPhrase companion all follow the instruction set. "that night" term propagation correctly copies only the Year term, since late_summer is not one of the Weekday/Day/Month/Year levels the rule names.

issues.reason: The split is real (one substance ends up under both the bare constant mist_light and a fresh sk_mist_light_1, so producing and attracting do not chain), but calling it a parse defect overstates it: Existential bars the bare class symbol "for a specific definite individual", so the definite "the mist-light" could not reuse mist_light, and every emitted atom is true and well-typed.

Names and casing directs that a name's kind be stated in one ordinary type atom "whether the kind word sits inside the name or beside it" (the Kestrel River -> (Member kestrel_river river)), and Core patterns licenses a type atom off "a kind word inside the name itself", so (Member middle_row row) is owed and its absence makes two otherwise identical names (Cliff Path, Middle Row) parse differently.

gaps_confirmed: a non-deictic season anchored to a stated year ("in the late summer of Year 1"): Time enumerates the structured terms Year/Month/Day/Weekday/Hour/Minute and lists seasons only as speech-anchored deictic constants (last_spring, next_summer), so no form is specified for a season of a named year and late_summer is invented
new_gaps: a definite NP whose only antecedent was introduced as a bare mass/kind constant ("the lantern produced mist-light" ... "The mist-light attracted nightmoths"): the specific definite must be a typed witness, but nothing licensed links that witness back to the earlier bare-constant mention, so one substance is recorded under two unrelated symbols; a licensed form would need an identity/portion link between a kind-filler mention and a later definite witness of the same stuff

"stay / remain + locative PP" when a reification trigger is present ("All the sky-cats stayed on the cliff-spires that night"): the time modifier licenses the reified Experiencer+Location state, but the continuative force of "stayed" still has no carrier there (the prompt itself registers the no-carrier note for the bare position route), so the rule is indistinguishable from "all the sky-cats were on the cliff-spires that night"
adjudication.defect_summary: Add the ordinary type atom (Member middle_row row) beside (Name middle_row "Middle Row") — the kind word sitting inside the name licenses and requires it, exactly as this same parse's (Member cliff_path path) does for "the Cliff Path".
adjudication.notes: I do not count the reviewer's second gap: "at the third watch" is covered by Time's rule that a deictic or named (non-calendar) time stays a bare symbol and composes with calendar terms, so third_watch is licensed rather than improvised. The rest of the parse holds up — the BeforeBy equinox gap, "that night" term propagation, the seventeen/handful count encodings, and the all-the-sky-cats per-member rule with its QuantifierPhrase companion.
